source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Place the client flat in a supine position to reduce respiratory effort","B":"Place the client upright in High-Fowler position to support lung expansion","C":"Place the client prone with the head turned to limit chest wall movement","D":"Place the client in Trendelenburg position to increase diaphragmatic pressure"}}
source_row.rationale: High-Fowler's position (sitting the client upright, typically at 60-90 degrees) allows for maximal lung expansion by reducing pressure from abdominal organs on the diaphragm and optimizing chest wall movement, making it the preferred position for a client experiencing respiratory distress, unless otherwise contraindicated.
source_row.source_detail: High-Fowler/tripod positioning promotes chest expansion and reduces work of breathing; 2nd ed. 2024, accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.stem: A client experiencing respiratory distress is most likely to benefit from which positioning?
